blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Every company says leadership is important, but only some actually invest in developing leaders. Leadership development is a long-term commitment — it takes years, not a single workshop. A one-day event can inspire people, but it rarely changes how they lead.

A strong programme rests on several pillars: self-awareness, people skills, strategic thinking, and the ability to make decisions under pressure. Good programmes mix coaching, mentoring, real stretch assignments and honest feedback from peers. Each of these does something the others cannot.

The goal is not to create clones of the CEO. It is to build a diverse pipeline of leaders who can step up when the company needs them, at every level. If you didn't build that pipeline today, you would not have the leaders you need tomorrow.

items.q: According to the text, how long does leadership development take?
items.why: "it takes years, not a single workshop" — é um compromisso de longo prazo.

items.q: Which pillars does a strong programme rest on?
options: Self-awareness, people skills, strategic thinking and decisions under pressure
items.why: O segundo parágrafo lista exatamente esses quatro pilares.

items.q: What is the stated goal of leadership development?
options: To build a diverse pipeline of leaders at every level
To create copies of the CEO
To reduce the number of managers
items.why: "It is to build a diverse pipeline of leaders who can step up… at every level."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A pipeline protects the company's future.
Mentoring adds something coaching alone cannot.
Leaders should not be clones of the CEO.
A single inspiring workshop is enough to develop leaders.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que desenvolvimento leva anos — um workshop isolado não basta.

items.q: "Each of these does something the others cannot" suggests that…
options: companies should pick just one method
the different methods complement each other and none is enough alone
coaching, mentoring, stretch assignments and feedback are interchangeable
items.why: Inferência: cada método cobre algo distinto, por isso a mistura é necessária.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentar o novo programa de liderança. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks, everyone. What you're looking at is a leadership development programme for our high-potential managers — the people we believe can run much bigger parts of this business in five years.

Let me be honest about why we're doing this now. Right now, when a senior role opens up, we scramble. We look outside, we pay a premium, and half the time the person doesn't fit our culture. If we had a real pipeline, succession would be far smoother, and we would promote from within with confidence.

So here's the design. Each manager gets a mentor from the executive team, a stretch assignment outside their comfort zone, and regular coaching. We're not chasing charisma. We want self-awareness, executive presence, and the ability to delegate and empower their teams — not do everyone's job for them.

One last thing. This only works if we hold people accountable, ourselves included. If we invested in this and then ignored it, we'd waste everyone's time. I'd rather we committed properly or not at all.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Who is the programme designed for?
options: High-potential managers who could run bigger parts of the business
items.why: "a leadership development programme for our high-potential managers."

items.q: What happens today when a senior role opens up, according to James?
options: They merge it with another role
They scramble and often hire outside at a premium
items.why: "we scramble. We look outside, we pay a premium…"

items.q: What does each manager receive in the programme?
options: A pay rise and a new title
A mentor, a stretch assignment and regular coaching
items.why: "a mentor from the executive team, a stretch assignment… and regular coaching."

items.q: What does James mean by "We're not chasing charisma"?
options: He values substance — self-awareness and presence — over a flashy personality
He thinks charisma is impossible to develop
items.why: Inferência: ele contrasta carisma com autoconhecimento e presença executiva reais.

items.q: Why does James stress accountability at the end?
options: To shift blame to the managers
Because a half-hearted commitment would waste everyone's effort
To warn that the programme is optional
Because he expects the programme to fail
items.why: Inferência: "If we invested… and then ignored it, we'd waste everyone's time" — só funciona com compromisso real.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A healthy leadership pipeline means we rarely have to hire from outside." A leadership pipeline is…
options: a supply of future leaders ready to step up
items.why: Leadership pipeline = funil de liderança: o fluxo de líderes em preparação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Great leaders show self-awareness — they know their ___ and their blind spots."
items.why: Self-awareness = autoconhecimento: reconhecer as próprias forças e pontos cegos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We gave her a stretch assignment — a project well beyond her current ___ — to accelerate her growth."
items.why: Stretch assignment = missão desafiadora, que tira a pessoa da zona de conforto.

items.q: "You'll never scale if you can't delegate." To delegate means to…
options: hand responsibility and tasks to others
items.why: Delegate = delegar: passar responsabilidade e tarefas ao time.

items.q: Executive presence is best described as…
options: clarity, confidence and credibility as a leader
items.why: Executive presence = presença executiva: clareza, confiança e credibilidade — não personalidade.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre desenvolvimento de líderes. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We need to step up and take on more responsibility." To step up means to…
items.why: Step up = assumir um desafio maior, dar um passo à frente.

items.q: "A good manager brings out the best in their team." This means they…
options: do the team's work for them
help people perform at their highest level
items.why: Bring out the best in = fazer as pessoas darem o seu melhor.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the leadership budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We agreed on the mentoring plan, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Coaching one manager for a week won't move the needle on our succession gap." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
